extracted.intended_audience: authors and writers seeking literary agents / users of a literary agent directory
extracted.subtask_description: Finding and evaluating literary agents (here: United Talent Agency) using an online directory and related author services; includes what information a directory entry should contain and what author support/coaching is offered. Aimed at authors preparing queries and selecting agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent directory listing fields / completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you register you’ll get instant access to the following: Agent bios for all agents at the United Talent Agency (UTA); AAR membership status; Personal email addresses; Mailing addresses; Agent photos; Preferred query letter methods (email, online form, postal mail); A link to the United Talent Agency (UTA) website; A map to the office of the United Talent Agency (UTA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page presents this bullet list as the essential data items the directory provides — implying these are the expected fields for a complete and useful agent profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searchability by book genre/category
rubrics_metrics.description: Search the directory by book genre/category (more than 100 categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directory usability criterion: ability to filter agents by specific genres/categories to find appropriate representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent genre specialties / represented categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The site enumerates many categories/genres (Children’s, Young Adult, Middle Grade, Chapter Book, Picture Book, Fiction, Crime, Fantasy, Historical, Horror, Mystery, Romance, Science Fiction, Thriller, Nonfiction, Memoir, New Age, Self-Help, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agent/profile should clearly indicate which of these genres they represent; genre alignment is a key criterion for matching authors to agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred query methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred query letter methods (email, online form, postal mail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directory entries include each agent's preferred query method, and authors are expected to follow that preference when querying — a compliance/formatting criterion for submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency/department track record and cross-platform rights development
rubrics_metrics.description: The department ... has placed books with every major publishing house and been unusually successful in developing books across digital and film platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating an agency or agent, an important quality criterion is their record of placements and ability to develop projects across publishing, digital, and film/TV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent/department leadership experience and notable roster
rubrics_metrics.description: Profiles of department leaders (e.g., Marc Gerald and Juliet Mushens) include prior industry roles, years of experience, and notable clients (Eminem, Brian Wilson, Isa Moskowitz, Sasha Grey, Jeffrey Brown, Jessie Burton, James Oswald).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent/leader bios should communicate experience, relevant prior roles, and successful clients — criteria for assessing agent credibility and fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directory accuracy / currency warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning! - Most literary agency directories (print and online) are outdated, incomplete, and riddled with mistakes. If you rely on those directories to find literary agents at the United Talent Agency (UTA), you’re going to hurt your chances of getting an agent to represent you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functions as a quality criterion for directory selection: prefer up-to-date, accurate resources; outdated/inaccurate directories are detrimental to an author's submission success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author support / coaching service areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Support areas listed: Book Development; Query Letter; Book Synopsis; Book Proposal; Author Platform; Agent Selection; Process/Strategy; Troubleshooting; Miscellaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the service categories authors can expect from the 1-on-1 coaching — useful checklist for authors to decide what help they need when preparing materials to approach agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims about consulting outcomes / success metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims: 'We've helped 400+ writers get book agents and/or traditional publishers.' 'Writers who've worked with Literary Agent Undercover ... have gotten six-figure book deals; been on the New York Times bestseller list; had their books adapted for TV, stage, and feature film; had their work licensed in 40+ countries; and sold many millions of books.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a consultant or service, these outcome claims act as advertised success metrics; authors should treat such claims as considerations but verify independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to update or add agent profile information
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary Agents: To update your profile on one of our websites, or to have us consider adding your information to our websites, Send Us an Email here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for agents: contact the site via the provided email to request profile updates or additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources provided upon registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Get instant access to our article/audio library, the official Directory of Literary Agents, and all our other resources for writers and authors; access to the Author Resource Library, Advice from Bestselling Authors (text and audio), Literary Agent Advice (text and audio), Insider Articles and Updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for directory/user value: registration should unlock educational resources, interviews, and practical guidance for querying and book development.
